title: 3. What Really Happened
description: Chapter 3 of 3 of “The Case of the Missing Star”. Read in order.

cover.alt: The Case of the Missing Star

illustration.alt: They uncover the star, examine the evidence, and test the loose bow.

lines: The children lift the striped cloth and find the whole star. Pico looks just as surprised as they are.
blocks.title: There it is!

lines: Nico holds the purple ring while Luna examines the ribbon. The star is undamaged, and the bow is loose.
blocks.title: Whole, but loose

lines: They gather the clues on the table beside the cart. One explanation should make sense of them all.
blocks.title: Putting it together

lines: Luna tests the loose bow by pulling one end. It slips open, showing how the star could come free.
blocks.title: Testing the bow

variants.retryFeedback: Watch what happens when the ribbon end is pulled.

variants.prompt: What does testing the loose bow show?

options.text: It could open when one end was pulled

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! It could open when one end was pulled.
variants.retryFeedback: Watch what happens when the ribbon end is pulled.

illustration.alt: Reconstruction: wind loosens the bow, the star falls and is covered, and the cart leaves traces.

lines: We look back to the beginning. Wind shook the ribbon while the cart stood directly underneath the decoration.
blocks.title: The wind returns

lines: The bow came undone, and the star fell into the cart. Pico was looking ahead and did not notice.
blocks.title: Falls into the cart

lines: A fold of cloth flipped over the falling star. That is how the decoration became hidden.
blocks.title: Covered by the cloth

lines: The cart left two muddy lines. Its trailing ribbon caught on a twig, leaving the little scrap behind.
blocks.title: The ribbon catches

variants.prompt: What hid the star inside the cart?
variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! A fold of cloth.
variants.retryFeedback: Follow this page’s four pictures in order.

options.text: The cloth moves, the cat ties the star, then wind arrives
The bow opens, the star falls, and the cloth covers it
The cart empties, the star flies up, and the bow tightens

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! The bow opens, the star falls, and the cloth covers it.
variants.retryFeedback: Follow this page’s four pictures in order.

illustration.alt: They return the star, tie a double knot, test it, and enjoy the party.

lines: Back in the present, Luna and Nico return the star to its hook. Its strange journey finally makes sense.
blocks.title: Back to the hook

lines: Luna ties a double knot while Nico supports the star. This time, they check the fastening together.
blocks.title: A double knot

lines: They give it a gentle tug. The flags still flutter, but the star remains firmly attached.
blocks.title: Testing it holds

lines: The party begins with the star back in place. Observing, comparing, and checking helped them solve the mystery.
blocks.title: The party begins!

variants.prompt: How does Luna fasten the star more securely?
variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! With a double knot.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the knot and what they do before the party starts.

variants.prompt: Why do they give the star a gentle tug at the end?

options.text: To check that their repair works

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! To check that their repair works.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the knot and what they do before the party starts.

ribbon.definition: A narrow strip of fabric used for tying or decorating.

bow.definition: A knot with loops that can be loosened by pulling an end.

hook.definition: A curved piece used to hang something.

scrap.definition: A small piece left or torn from something.

explanation.definition: An account of how or why something happened.

decoration.definition: Something used to make a place look special.

fastening.definition: A way of holding something in place.
